'''Tasoltan Tazretovich Basiev''' ({{langx|ru|Тасолтан Тазретович Басиев}}; 1947 – 2012) was a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] and [[Russia]]n scientist and [[professor]] in the field of [[photonics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ras.ru/win/db/show_per.asp?P=.id-60506.ln-ru.dl-.pr-inf.uk-12|title=Басиев Т.Т. – Общая информация|website=www.ras.ru|access-date=2018-05-23}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Basiev was born in 1947 in [[Moscow]].

He graduated from the [[Moscow Power Engineering Institute]] in 1972. After graduation, he started working at the [[Lebedev Physical Institute|Lebedev Physical Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1984, Basiev went defended his doctoral dissertation "Selective laser spectroscopy of activated crystals and glasses".

He created fluoride laser [[Ceramic nanoparticle|nano-ceramics]] and the [[Single crystal|mono crystal]] laser, which is a solid-state laser with an energy of more than 100 Joules (100 ns), that had a peak power of more than 200 GW (500 fs). He developed new SRS crystals and lasers. He established the quadruple mechanism of coherent entanglement in nanoclusters and weakened coherence. Those are methods for [[nanophotonics]] of RE ions in laser crystals and glasses.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ras.ru/win/DB/show_per.asp?P=.id-60506.ln-ru.dl-.pr-inf.uk-11|title=Басиев Т.Т. – Общая информация|website=www.ras.ru|access-date=2018-05-23}}</ref>

He is the author and co-author of 412 scientific works, 36 of which are reviews, 4 monographs and earned 28 patents.<ref name=":0" />

== Recognition ==
Basiev was a member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences|RAS]] Commission on Prizes for Young Scientists of the Russian Federation, the Scientific Council of the Russian Academy of Sciences on Spectroscopy of Atoms and Molecules, the editorial board of Optical Materials and Quantum Electronics and a Ph.D. Member of the [[The Optical Society|American Optical Society]].
